title: fix(spec): correct both $between-endpoint entries' carrier claims and detectors
body:
Fixes #19523

Clause-②: no

The shipped ADR-0087 semantic entry `filter-between-blank-endpoint-refused` told an upgrader that `FieldOperatorsSchema.safeParse` **and re-saving the document** both make the sweep mechanical, over a carrier list of six slots. Re-saving is mechanical on **none** of the stored carriers, so an upgrader who re-saved every dashboard, dataset and report found no blank endpoint refused and concluded the sweep was done. This corrects the entry's `surface`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` to say what is actually judged where.

No behaviour moves: no schema or accept set is touched, and no export is added, removed or retyped; what moves in `dist` is the prose of the two step-18 entries the exported `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` carries. What changes is what the document tells a human to do.

## Why this needs the registry, and why it publishes

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/**` is **generator input only** — it is not in this package's `files[]`, and nothing imports it but the generator and two pin tests — while `registry.ts` is what `chain.ts` and `index.ts` import and what `dist` is built from. So a corrected entry alone reaches no consumer; the regenerated registry is what carries it. That is the whole reason this card needed a second round.

`registry.ts` here is **regenerated, never hand-edited**: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry` reproduces the committed file byte-for-byte (blob `15927d08a2dbc08aa0d668e2094133c038b6b4a2` at head `242e102b74`, before and after the run; `check:migration-registry` reports current at 231 semantic, 207 retired-key, 183 retired-def). The blob this sentence cited in round 1, `363ca1de4a`, was the registry at `4e3a6373fa`; the file was regenerated twice since.

## The contested claim, re-derived rather than inherited

Card #19523's own leg 2 asserted that the `view` carrier **does** refuse a blank `$between` endpoint. Measured against `origin/main` at `c120dbdfb8`, on this branch, 2026-09-22T22:0xZ — it does not:

`ViewFilterRuleSchema.safeParse({ field: 'close_date', operator: 'between', value: V })`

| V | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `['2026-01-01','2026-12-31']` | green — dark control, a good range passes |
| `['2026-01-01','']` | **green** — a blank endpoint is admitted |
| `['2026-01-01']` | refused at `value` — firing control, arity is judged |
| `['2026-01-01',{ $field:'x' }]` | refused at `value` — firing control, the union rejects an object |

The same four verdicts hold through a fully-green `ListView` document at `filter.0.value` (the dark-control document parses with zero issues, so the reading is the value judgment and not a key refusal). `checkViewFilterRuleValueShape` judges `Array.isArray(value) && value.length === 2` and nothing else for the pair operators — arity, not blankness.

## What does refuse, with controls

Every row below: blank MIN, blank MAX and an absent bound refused; a good range and `['0','9']` green (the rule is blankness, not falsiness).

- `FieldOperatorsSchema` — refuses at `$between.1` / `$between.0`, naming the MAX / MIN bound.
- `RangeOperatorSchema` — same refusal, same paths.
- `NormalizedFilterSchema` — refuses at `$and.0.close_date.$between.N`.
- **Execution door** — `assertListComparandShapes` (`@objectstack/objectql`, wired at `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:866`, delegating to `packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-shape.ts`) throws `code: INVALID_FILTER`, `status: 400`, naming the index and the side. The corrected prescription rests on this door, and it is real.

## Publishing reach — measured, with a positive and a dark control

Two builds of `@objectstack/spec`, counted over the four `dist` bundles in the `files[]` entry `dist` (`dist/index.js`, `dist/index.mjs`, `dist/browser/index.js`, `dist/browser/index.mjs`):

| leg | old sentence | new sentence | entry id (dark control) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| registry at `51687e1440` (entry corrected, registry NOT regenerated) | **4** | 0 | 8 |
| registry regenerated (this branch) | **0** | **4** | 8 |

The positive control moves 4 → 0 and the corrected text 0 → 4, while the dark control holds at 8 in both legs — so the grep instrument is live and the four files carry this entry in both states. Restore was verified twice by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`. This is why the changeset is a `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and why `skip-changeset` would be wrong.

## `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` cannot move from this card

`packages/spec/scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts` loops majors `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR+1 … PROTOCOL_MAJOR` = 17…17, while this entry is step **18**. The entry id appears in the guide **0** times; a step-17 entry id appears **1** time in the same grep, so the instrument is live rather than dead. `check:upgrade-guide` exits 0.

## Amendment round — the corrected surface had one false clause of its own

The first correction described the `FilterConditionSchema` carriers as a loose record intersected with the `$and` / `$or` / `$not` shape **that never judges an operator map**. That clause is false, and the sibling entry `filter-preset-ordering-comparand-refused` contradicts it in its own surface. The mechanism is `.superRefine(checkBarePresetOrderingComparands)` on `FilterConditionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts:1717`).

Re-derived in this worktree at `3335eaad1f` against the freshly built `dist` (`packages/spec/dist/data`, `packages/spec/dist/ui`), 2026-09-22T23:17:35Z:

- `$gt` with `today` / `this_month` / `last_7_days` / `yesterday` / `this_week` is **REFUSED** at `close_date.$gt`, with `$gt: '2026-01-01'` green as the firing control and `$gt: 'last_7_daysX'` green as a dark control.
- `$between: ['today', '2026-12-31']` is **REFUSED** at `close_date.$between.0`, and `['today', 'this_month']` at both `.0` and `.1`.
- `$and: 'nope'` is refused at `$and`; an unrecognised `$` key and arbitrary junk keys stay green (the loose record).
- **BLANKNESS and ARITY are what these carriers never judge**: `['2026-01-01', '']` is green, so is `['', '']`, and so are one-element, three-element and empty `$between` arrays.

Through an otherwise green `DashboardWidgetSchema` document (`id`, `type`, `dataset`, `values`, `filter`) the same split holds: `['today', '2026-12-31']` is refused at `filter.close_date.$between.0` and `$gte: 'last_30_days'` at `filter.close_date.$gte`, while the blank endpoint on that same widget, the arity cases and the dark control `['todayish', '2026-12-31']` all parse green.

⇒ the entry now says the narrower thing — those carriers never judge a `$between` endpoint **for blankness or for arity** — and names the rule that IS live on them, so the correction cannot be read as the inverted defect.

**Reach of the amendment**, re-measured on two real builds over the same four `dist` bundles, counting the full removed sentence (`operator map. Every one of those documents parses GREEN`) rather than the bare substring: build at `4e3a6373fa` gave positive control **4**, both new sentences **0**, dark control **0**; build at `3335eaad1f` after `gen:migration-registry` gave positive control **0**, each new sentence **4**, dark control **0**. The changeset gained one bullet stating the same live rule, so the text that ships as `CHANGELOG.md` is not left describing only what is NOT judged.

## Third round — the sibling entry carried the identical clause, and it is corrected here

The previous round's acceptance note reported that `filter-between-field-reference-endpoint-refused` spelled the same false claim in its own words, and left it untouched under orders. The standing `Claim:` on #19523 covers any sibling semantic entry measured to carry that wording, so this round corrects it.

**Premise re-verified before editing, against a freshly built `dist` and never from `src`.** `FilterConditionSchema` carries `.superRefine(checkBarePresetOrderingComparands)` (`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts:1717`). Read out of `packages/spec/dist/data/index.mjs` and `packages/spec/dist/ui/index.mjs` at branch head `c06eec4029`:

| document | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `{ close_date: { $between: [{ $field: 'contract.start' }, '2026-12-31'] } }` | green |
| `{ close_date: { $between: ['2026-01-01'] } }` / `['a','b','c']` / `[]` | green — arity is not judged |
| `{ close_date: { $between: ['last_30_days', '2026-12-31'] } }` | **refused** at `close_date.$between.0` |
| `{ close_date: { $gte: 'last_30_days' } }` | **refused** at `close_date.$gte` |

Through an otherwise-green `DashboardWidgetSchema` document (`id`, `type`, `dataset`, `values`, `filter`) the same split holds, at `filter.close_date.$between.0` and `filter.close_date.$gt`, with the two literal-endpoint controls green. So "never judges an operator map" is false on this entry exactly as it was on its sibling.

**The correction.** The clause now names what those carriers genuinely never judge — a `$between` endpoint **for a COLUMN REFERENCE or for ARITY** — and names the preset-ordering rule that IS live on them, pointing at `filter-preset-ordering-comparand-refused`, so it cannot be read as the inverted defect. `acceptanceCriteria` stops offering "those slots are `FilterConditionSchema`" as the reason such a document parses green. All three entries in this family now describe the same carrier set the same way.

`registry.ts` was regenerated with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry` and never hand-edited; `check:migration-registry` reports `231 semantic, 207 retired-key, 183 retired-def` current.

**Reach**, counted with `grep -o | wc -l` over `dist/index.js`, `dist/index.mjs`, `dist/browser/index.js` and `dist/browser/index.mjs`, on two real builds:

| string | before | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `shape that never judges an operator map` (removed text) | 4 (1 per bundle) | **0** |
| bare `never judges an operator map` (the carrier count this PR was measured by) | 4 | **0** |
| `a $between endpoint for a COLUMN REFERENCE or for ARITY` (positive control, unique to this entry) | 0 | **4** (1 per bundle) |
| `close_date $between { $field: "contract.start" } and 2026-12-31` (second positive control, unique to this entry) | 0 | **4** |
| `whose one refinement judges bare date-range preset comparands` (acceptanceCriteria control) | 0 | **4** |
| `a $between endpoint for a COLUMN REFERENCE or for BLANKNESS` (dark control) | 0 | **0** |

The dark control holds at 0 on both sides, so the instrument can report zero; neither positive control is the bare substring several entries used to share.

**No fourth carrier.** At head `242e102b74`, `git grep -F 'judges an operator map'` reads **1** line repo-wide, carrying 2 occurrences: `.changeset/19523-blank-endpoint-entry-carriers.md:14`, the changeset quoting the removed clause and naming the reach grep's search string. No entry carries it, and the four `dist` bundles read 0 (control in the same `git grep`: `DOES judge an operator map` reads 4 occurrences). The other `never judges` hits in `packages/spec/src` are `18.filter-text-operator-declared-type-refused.ts:19` and its generated mirror `registry.ts:8664`, about an RLS / sharing / tenant predicate composed onto the AST after the engine door, and a doc comment at `system/job.zod.ts:24` about a column nothing reads back: different subjects, not this clause.

**Changeset.** The existing `patch` changeset named only the blank-endpoint entry, so the compiled `CHANGELOG.md` would not have told an upgrader that this entry moved as well. It gains one bullet carrying the same measurement and the same reach table, and its opening sentence now names both entries. `Clause-②: no` is unchanged: no schema or accept set moves, and no export is added, removed or retyped.

## The red on `Test Core (3/6)` at `c06eec4029` is neither this PR's diff nor the base move

Diagnosed from the job's own log. Run 35799036431, job 106984977747 (`Test Core (3/6)`, head `c06eec4029`, `completed: failure`). An earlier round's REST read of that log was refused at this container's egress gateway, and this section recorded it as not retrieved; the log **is** readable through the GitHub MCP `get_job_logs` tool, and round 4 read it: the last 400 of its 18,899 lines, which hold the shard's failure block, its totals and turbo's run summary.

- **The one failed test** (`Failed Tests 1`): `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template-date-offset-dst.test.ts` → `#14852 {TODAY() +/- n} resolves on one calendar, across DST transitions` → `spring-forward: Asia/Jerusalem @ 2026-03-27T23:30:00Z (Sat 2026-03-28 02:30 IDT) {TODAY() - 1}` → `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.` at `template-date-offset-dst.test.ts:138:9`. A timeout, not a failed assertion.
- **Totals:** `Test Files  1 failed | 140 passed (141)`, `Tests  1 failed | 1689 passed (1690)`, `Duration  193.68s (transform 31.71s, setup 0ms, import 498.00s, tests 27.24s, environment 53ms)`: 498 s importing against 27 s running tests.
- **Turbo's summary** names one failed task: `Failed: @objectstack/service-automation#test`.

Measured by earlier rounds, and consistent with that log:

- `@objectstack/service-automation` at branch head `c06eec4029`, with its dependency closure built: **141 test files, 1690 tests, exit 0**, the same 141 / 1690 population the failing log reports.
- **The exact generation CI tested.** A `pull_request` run tests head merged into base. `git merge-tree --write-tree c06eec4029 2bdb81f8ad` writes tree `677a82c6947d2a9b8e1ea023bf762617c44ead6d`; that tree was materialised in a throwaway worktree and its own `git write-tree` reads the identical sha. On it: **141 files, 1690 tests, exit 0**.
- **The base move cannot reach this package.** `c120dbdfb8..2bdb81f8ad` is one commit touching `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, its test and a changeset, and it changes **0** `.describe()` strings. Built both ways, `dist/index.js`, `dist/index.mjs`, `dist/browser/index.js` and `dist/browser/index.mjs` are **byte-identical**; the only differing files in the whole built JS tree are `dist/ui/index.js` and `dist/ui/index.mjs`, differing only in preserved TSDoc prose — and `packages/services/service-automation/src` imports `@objectstack/spec/ui` **zero** times.
- **The added changeset line cannot reach it either.** This package's tests are package-local; the single read that leaves a test file is `flow-activation-ledger.test.ts` reading its own `./engine.ts`. The one `.changeset`-reading test inside `@objectstack/spec` lists `.changeset/` as an *excluded prefix*.
And one reading of this round's own: `c06eec4029` is an ancestor of `e43b3c0a99` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0), and at `e43b3c0a99` all seven `Test Core` check-runs read `success`.

⇒ the conclusion stands, and the log now corroborates it: a 5000 ms timeout on a DST date-arithmetic case, in a run that spent 498 s importing, is a non-deterministic failure on that runner, not a property of the tree. ⛔ No test was skipped, disabled or quarantined, and `origin/main` was **not** merged into the branch.

**The candidate named before the log was read is falsified for this red.** `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.test.ts:2356-2364` is not the failed test; the log's one failed test is the DST case above. That file's own defect, a wall-clock bound that cannot fail on the regression it documents, does not depend on this red and stays filed as **#19766**.

## Fourth round — every scope word in the changeset, checked against a reading

Head `242e102b74`, one commit on `e43b3c0a99`, touching only `.changeset/19523-blank-endpoint-entry-carriers.md` (+5/−5). The two entries, `registry.ts` and every source file are byte-unchanged, so the at-tier record at `e43b3c0a99` still describes them; this head owes its own record for the changeset.

Readings against a freshly built `dist`, resolved through the package's own `exports` (`@objectstack/spec/data`, `/ai`, `/ui` → `packages/spec/dist/*/index.js`), each with a dark control:

| changeset sentence | reading | now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the preset rule is refused "on **exactly** this carrier set" (NB-2) | false: `QuerySchema` refuses `where: { close_date: { $gt: 'today' } }` at `where.close_date.$gt`, `BlueprintSummaryOperationsSchema` refuses it as `filter` at `filter.close_date.$gt`; `$gt: '2026-01-01'` green on both | "refused on this carrier set", plus a sentence naming both: the refinement rides the schema, not these slots |
| the removed clause has "no carrier … anywhere in the tree" (NB-3) | false on the literal reading: the changeset quotes it | "no entry carries it any more: in the tree it survives only in this changeset, which quotes the removed clause" |
| "no schema, accept set or export is touched" | false on the literal reading: the exported `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` carries both edited entries, and their prose moves in `dist` | no schema or accept set touched; no export added, removed or retyped (`check:api-surface` unchanged); every line the PR edits in `registry.ts` is a string literal inside step 18's two entries |
| "the corrected prose reaches consumers only through it" | false on the literal reading once this changeset compiles into the shipped `CHANGELOG.md`, which quotes pieces of that prose | "of the two, only the registry carries the corrected prose into `dist`" |
| an upgrader "found nothing refused" | contradicted by the changeset's own preset bullet for a stored preset comparand | "found no blank endpoint refused" |

Scope words kept, each with its reading:

- **"mechanical on none of the stored carriers" / "every stored metadata carrier"** (blankness not judged at save). Each of the eight `FilterConditionSchema` slot declarations behind the seven named carriers (`DashboardWidget.filter`, `GlobalFilterOptionsFrom.filter`, `DatasetMeasure.filter`, `Dataset.filter`, `JoinedReportBlock.runtimeFilter`, `Report.runtimeFilter`, `Field.relatedListFilter`, `Field.summaryOperations.filter`) raises no issue at the slot path for `$between: ['2026-01-01', '']`, while refusing the preset `$gt` at that same path (firing control). `ViewFilterRuleSchema` is green on the blank endpoint and refuses a one-element value. No stored slot in `packages/spec/src` is typed `FieldOperatorsSchema`, `RangeOperatorSchema` or `NormalizedFilterSchema`: in non-test source outside `filter.zod.ts` and the migration prose, the one non-comment use of any of them is a type-level assertion in `recursive-schema-input-assertions.ts`.
- **"never judge … for blankness or for arity"** and **"… for a COLUMN REFERENCE or for ARITY"**. `FilterConditionSchema` is green on a blank MAX, both blank, a `null` endpoint, arity 0 / 1 / 3, a `{ $field }` endpoint and a blank endpoint under `$and`; it refuses a preset `$between` endpoint and `$and: 'nope'` (firing controls).
- **"only `entries/README.md` ships"**. `npm pack --dry-run` lists 2031 files; the only one under `src/migrations/` is `src/migrations/entries/README.md`.
- **"nothing imports it but the generator and two pin tests"**. `git grep` finds two test imports of `migrations/entries`, and the generator `build-migration-registry.ts` reads the directory with `readdirSync`.

⚠️ **Why the rewrite does not say "every carrier of `FilterConditionSchema`".** `EngineQueryOptionsSchema.where` names the schema inside `z.union([z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()), FilterConditionSchema])`. The loose-record branch answers first, so `{ close_date: { $gt: 'today' } }` parses **green** there (firing control: `where: 'nope'` refused, `invalid_union`). The rule is live on a slot that parses through the schema, not on every slot that names it.

Verification at `242e102b74`, every exit code captured before any pipe:

- `pnpm check:empty-changeset` → exit 0; `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base c120dbdfb8` → exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --self-test` → exit 0 (365 assertions); `--base c120dbdfb8` → exit 0; `--event` with this PR's payload → exit 0, level axis reads `Clause-②: no`.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` → exit 0 (9239 text files, no raw control bytes).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` → 80 derived; `--ran` reconciliation: **79 run, exit 0; 1 NOT MEASURED; 0 UNRUN**. The NOT MEASURED one is `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, exit 3 `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: it needs a repo-wide build, which is CI's run. ⛔ Not a pass.
- The five artifact-roster gates whose roster sits under a touched directory (`check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`) → all exit 0.
- No package is touched, so this round owes no package build or test.

## Acceptance notes

- The sibling carrier reported here last round **is corrected in this PR** — see the third-round section above. The bare substring `never judges an operator map` now reads **0** in `dist`; `git grep -F 'judges an operator map'` reads 1 line repo-wide, the changeset's own quotation of the removed clause.
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.test.ts:2356-2364` asserts `expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(100)` over a real `Date.now()` window as a proxy for "both branches ran in parallel". The test's own comment puts the fully-sequential path at `10+10=20ms`, which is also under 100 — so the assertion cannot fail on the regression it documents, while it can fail on a slow or contended runner. Out of scope for this card and deliberately not touched here; filed as **#19766**.
- `scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs` classified `HTTP 403 Access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy`, returned by the egress proxy for the `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` mint path, as `ratelimit`, and wrote a 30-minute fleet-wide stop marker refusing every write by that identity. `GET /rate_limit` read `limit 15000, remaining 14899` at that moment, so no limit was in play. Out of scope, not touched here. ⛔ Not re-filed: it is **#19696**, closed `not_planned` by triage under ruling #202 letter B (a `tooling` card needs an `Unblocks:` product card or a named customer-visible surface), with its firings recorded there.
